novelty.justification: The claim hypothesizes that "subject-enrichment step is largely language-agnostic, while only the final attribute-token surfacing is language-specific," presenting this as a new mechanistic decomposition of multilingual factual recall. For the search constructs "multilingual factual recall subject enrichment language independent," "cross-lingual factual recall activation patching," and "language-agnostic retrieval language-specific object extraction," the closest work is How Do Multilingual Language Models Remember Facts? (2024), which already reports through intermediate-representation patching that subject enrichment is language-independent while object extraction is language-dependent; Lost in Multilinguality (ACL 2025) likewise locates language-independent factual concepts before a final language-specific transition. The step to this claim is therefore essentially equivalent prior work rather than a direct transfer or natural extension: even its proposed shared-retrieval/specific-surfacing boundary and patching characterization already appear in the closest paper.
